newsitem.title: UK: UK's ABI says consumer confidence boosts Q1 sales.
newsitem.headline: UK's ABI says consumer confidence boosts Q1 sales.

text.p: The Association of British Insurers (ABI) said on Wednesday first quarter sales of new life insurance and pension policies reflected rising consumer confidence in the state of the UK economy.
Sales of new life and pension policies increased 10 percent to 4.5 billion stg in the first three months of 1996, the sixth consecutive quarter of year-on-year increases.
"With rising real incomes, people are doing the sensible thing and putting more money aside in long-term investments to help secure their future," said the ABI's director general Mark Boleat.
The dominance of new single premium business was explained by people looking for value-for-money and maximum flexibility, said Boleat.
Premium income for new life insurance was up eight percent on the same year-earlier period at three billion stg.
New annual premiums increased seven percent to 300 million stg and single premiums eight percent to 2.7 billion stg.
Premium income for individual pensions rose 12 percent to 1.4 billion stg. New annual premiums were 300 million stg, up five percent, while single premiums rose 14 percent to 1.1 billion stg.
